entities.summary: The Marble Collegiate Church, founded in 1628, is one of the oldest continuous Protestant congregations in North America. The congregation, which is part of two denominations in the Reformed tradition—the United Church of Christ and the Reformed Church in America—is located at 272 Fifth Avenue at the corner of West 29th Street in the NoMad neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. It was built in 1851–54 and was designed by Samuel A. Warner in Romanesque Revival style with Gothic trim. The façade is covered in Tuckahoe marble, for which the church, originally called the Fifth Avenue Church, was renamed in 1906.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the oldest continuous Protestant congregations in North America, the Marble Collegiate Church has played a significant role in shaping American religious history and culture. Its enduring presence has influenced generations of reformers and shaped the development of Reformed traditions in the United States.
